_README: Promoted, tracked copy of the run whose numbers are cited. Regenerate with `python -m crest.analysis.promote_leaderboard --run <run_dir>`. summary.json is NOT a substitute: it lacks the primary endpoint, the provenance and the caveats.

provenance.judge_protocol: full-panel (same-family as covariate); blind; median aggregation

primary_endpoint.definition: min(New, Useful, Surprising), graded on the 1-10 scale

caveats: NO RANKING CLAIM IS MADE. On the science run, per-axis judge severity (3.32/3.20/3.74) EXCEEDED the entire between-entrant spread (2.06), so an ordering is not identifiable from a run of this design. This table is not a leaderboard.

DIFFERENT ITEM SET AND DIFFERENT JUDGE PROMPT from result/leaderboard.json. These are the 50 AI/ML items, and this is the FIRST run scored under JUDGE_PROMPT_VERSION v2 (hash e2ce119c); the science run is v1/null. The two files' numbers are NOT comparable in either direction.

n IS UNEQUAL AND NOT MISSING AT RANDOM: claude_shallow/openai_deepresearch/openai_shallow n=50, gemini_shallow n=47, gemini_deepresearch_max n=46. The 7 missing records are provider failures concentrated in the two Google arms (4x flaky 400 'invalid argument' on the deep-research preview surface, 2x ServerError, 1x ReadTimeout), so absence correlates with the provider, not with the items.

gemini_shallow DID NOT BROWSE. It returned ZERO web searches on essentially every item (verified three ways: the google_search tool IS attached, 0 grounding-metadata parse failures, and tokens.input_tool_use == 0). Part of its low score reflects answering from parametric memory rather than lower creativity, and its citations are scraped from answer text rather than verified grounding chunks.

THE ENDPOINT IS LARGELY HARD-RULE COMPLIANCE. corr(min(N,U,S), Useful) = 0.957 on this run. Useful is ~85% explained by a single binary ('did any judge cite a rule violation'): clean judge rows average 8.63, citing rows 2.84. Audited 2026-07-31: only 9.5% of the 702 hard rules across both item files are creativity-relevant, and those rules account for 0.5% of the violations cited on this run.

THE GATE IS A JUDGE-IDENTITY EFFECT ON THIS ITEM SET. Rule-gate firing rate by judge: judge_openai 77.3%, judge_anthropic 63.8%, judge_google 4.3%. Judge identity explains 40.3% of gate variance versus 30.1% for answer identity, and Useful's one-way ICC(1,k) is NEGATIVE here. Do not read per-entrant Useful differences as answer quality without accounting for this.
1 truncated record (claude_shallow) is included and flagged; filter on `truncated` before any length-sensitive analysis.

Retrieval was LIVE provider web search. Not contamination-controlled; no frozen index exists. The run directory is gitignored, so per-record judge rows and transcripts are not distributed and this file cannot be recomputed from a fresh clone.
